Delegation-to-tool skills that saved on Sonnet (+53%) continue to cost more on Opus when Opus arm A is already efficient at the underlying task cold.

haiku.notes: Save rate 57% on Haiku — HIGHEST of the three models, matches the Sonnet pattern (53%) and inverts Opus's -14% cost-more. Haiku arm A re-implemented a JSONL walker like Sonnet did (63K) — the smaller model lacks Opus's 'just write a Python helper' shortcut. Arm B used 4 tool uses to invoke the prescribed scan.mjs cleanly. Strong evidence that delegation-to-tool skills are most valuable for the LEAST capable model.

opus.notes: Clean re-baseline 2026-05-26. Save rate 39% — prior 51% narrowed; clean arm A 9K cheaper (59K→50K). Recipe still saves but less dramatically. The six-step pipeline-discovery walk continues to compress arm A's cold exploration.

haiku.notes: Save rate dropped from 52% (Sonnet) to 33% (Haiku) — the only sample skill where Haiku saves substantially less than Sonnet. Haiku arm B used 10 tool uses (vs Sonnet's 2, Opus's 2) — the smaller model needed more turns to execute the prescribed pipeline. The recipe still helps but less than for capable models, because Haiku spends more tokens per recipe step. This is the predicted Haiku failure mode showing up: smaller model can follow the recipe but pays per-turn overhead.
